# Synthetic provider-format and chart fixtures

All maintained fixture data are constructed by `scripts/test-fixtures/generate.py` from explicit scenario definitions, team-code catalogues and the parser contracts. The generator uses only the Python standard library and **never reads captured provider responses**. It performs no network requests. Fixture files and `manifest.json` are committed for independent offline builds.

```sh
python scripts/test-fixtures/generate.py
python scripts/test-fixtures/generate.py --check
python -m unittest discover -s tests/fixtures -v
```

`--check` compares regenerated bytes without writing them. Edit the generator, not its outputs. `manifest.json` binds every generated file to its SHA-256. The manifests' synthetic marker and this provenance apply even where an existing test consumer expects a bare array/CSV rather than a wrapper object.

## What the scenarios prove

- Four sports' qualification catalogues: alias normalization, market completeness, duplicate/missing teams, fractional depth, maximum-spread boundaries, one-sided bounds, settlement, archives/pagination, correction and expiry.
- MLB same-day schedule reconciliation: independently constructed event/team IDs and prices, both canonical rule grammars, strict scheduling/identity/status/deadline controls and importer/page wiring. Fixed parser-required contract language is a compatibility reference, not an observed response or a publisher license grant.
- Pro-hype schedules: full season lengths, completed counters, score/status contradictions, abbreviated rounds and play-in labels, best-of series progression and qualification-only Stakes and ignored seeding metadata. Synthetic league schedules deliberately do not assert a historically consistent real league.
- MoneyPuck rankings: constructed row order, alias coverage, quoted CSV handling, publication timezone/season/age and rank-based quality. Synthetic forecast values are not provider predictions.
- NHL Power Rankings Guru: independently constructed single-page HTML, canonical team-page identities, explicit positions, season/Eastern publication metadata, malformed-batch controls, daily admission and same-source Quality fallback. Constant synthetic forecast columns prove they are ignored; no provider ranking values, markup capture or artwork are bundled.
- NHL constructive seeding: 1,344 invented contest identities give each of 32 teams 84 matchups. Test-local source envelopes and hypothetical completions exercise retained positioning metadata, completed/overtime records, unsafe-input rejection and registered qualification-only capture/page propagation. No observed schedule or result is transcribed; the original qualification and ranking controls remain independent.
- NBA bounded seeding: 1,200 invented known contests give each of 30 teams 80 published matchups; no missing fixtures are added. Test-local records and independent assignments exercise all nine unknown-slot win-count combinations, actual additional published games, strict positioning metadata, Cup independence, unsafe-source controls and registered qualification-only capture/page propagation. A separate Fraction/Decimal oracle verifies the literal tuple; no live schedule, rank or quote is transcribed.
- MoneyPuck qualification: invented 32-team model values, marker/HTML/schema and exact game-ID/season joins, including IDs whose prefix cannot establish season. Model/market isolation, daily shared budget, denial persistence, race/high-water/freshness and atomicity protections remain tested.
- MLB scoreboard (`MlbScoreboard/espn-basic.json`): nine invented contests (`991300101`–`991300109`) with invented team IDs. They cover explicit home and away sides, one listed away-first, a final without a bottom ninth, an 11-inning final, a doubleheader pair, a postponed game and its makeup, a canceled game, a rain delay, and a suspended game that resumes under the same ID on the next date. Six observations of the two scoreboard dates cover in-order, partial, out-of-order and future frames, then the resumption and makeup results. `servedAt` is the fake clock and `responseDate` is the source time. An authored `null` inning list, hit count or error count is omitted from the board, so absence stays distinct from a recorded zero. Each board carries its expected identities, statuses and lines. Backend tests serve each board through the real ESPN scoreboard fetch and deserialization, deny every other request, and report a corrupted identity, side, nesting, status or line. The current fetch reads neither observation time and its typed model has no hits, errors or inning lines, so the backend tests compare those lines in the raw JSON, and only the fixture test checks observation order.
- MLB rich frames (`MlbScoreboard/rich-frames.json`): normalized Nailbiter rendering inputs for half-inning, count, bases, runners and matchup. A `null` fact is unknown and a zero is a recorded zero. These frames are not an ESPN situation schema, and no ingestion supplies them.
- Chart histories: two invented staircase cases (`990000001`, `990000002`) with microsecond timestamps, 300/320 samples, explicit eligibility flags and a ten-sample near-certain bound tail. HTTP tests verify every chart field, independent home/away parsing, latest-100 API behavior, ordering and expiry. A rational-number oracle integrates the constructed steps independently of the production scorer.

The CFB case alternates 0.5/0.75 every 40 samples, then ends with 0.995. The NFL case alternates 0.2/0.8 every 35 samples. Every nonzero movement exceeds the reversal threshold; independent analytic totals are **20.83333** and **56.16**, not old empirical calibration observations. Existing short-path threshold/jitter/symmetry/saturation tests remain additional independent controls.

## Boundaries

Team names/codes and provider route/schema spellings identify compatibility cases. Old numeric game IDs retained in some file names are opaque test identifiers, not assertions that those games had the constructed scores, quotes, schedules or results. All publication/observation times here are fixed clocks. URLs in mock envelopes match requested routes but are never fetched by the fixture generator/tests.

Historical captures and their original assertions remain private archival evidence; they are not part of this public suite or required for its CI. Replacing them loses live-contract corroboration: passing synthetic tests does **not** prove provider availability, actual response shape, sustained coverage or current semantic conformance. The MLB scoreboard fixtures validate the implemented contracts only, not current provider conformance, field availability, authorization or live latency. New provider access requires its own authorization and cannot be inferred from this suite.

Generated fixture changes must preserve each covered failure mode. In particular, adjust a boundary mutation when a new synthetic baseline quote changes; do not weaken the assertion or production acceptance policy just to make the replacement pass.
